name: Hand Horn
description: A natural horn with a crook and a hand in the bell. Notes the tube gives are bright and open; every other key is stopped by the hand, and is darker the further it moved.

params.name: Crook
params.description: The tube in use. Its own notes sound open and the keys between them are stopped, so each crook puts the bright and the dark keys in other places.

params.name: Hand
params.description: How far the hand corrects. At zero every key falls to the nearest note of the tube at its own pitch, all open; at full every key is in tune and stopped as it needs.

params.name: Lip
params.description: How far the lips alone bend an open note before the hand has to help. Wide leaves more keys open, and the ones pulled upward are a little thinner.

params.name: Shadow
params.description: How dark, small and nasal the hand makes a stopped note. At zero stopped and open notes have one colour.

params.name: Blow
params.description: How bright the horn is blown. Low is a soft round hum; high turns brassy as a note swells or is played harder.

params.name: Breath
params.description: Air heard around the tone. The hand covers it along with the note.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a note takes to speak. The highs come in after the lows, and low notes always take a little longer.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a note takes to fade once its key is let go. It darkens as it fades.

params.name: Play
params.description: Solo is one horn: keys that overlap slide into each other and the last key held wins. Chords is a horn to each key, six at most.

params.name: Lip slide
params.description: Time a slide takes between overlapping keys in Solo. The lips climb every note of the tube on the way and stop a moment on each.

params.name: Rip
params.description: A rough start on every fresh note. It scoops up from the next lower note of the tube with a crack on the way; high starts lower and takes longer.

params.name: Tremble
params.description: The hand opening and closing in the bell. Pitch and colour move together: lower and darker, then higher and more open.

params.name: Tremble rate
params.description: How fast the hand opens and closes. It is heard only with Tremble up.

params.name: Distance
params.description: How far off the bell is. Farther is softer and duller, with the ground and the walls answering more than the horn itself.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Places low notes to the left and high notes to the right, and widens what comes back in Distance. At zero all is in the middle.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. No recording, sample, circuit or measurement of an instrument was used: it is the textbook physics of a horn with no valves, whose partials stand at whole multiples of the crook's fundamental, with a hand in the bell that lowers a note as it closes. The rule is exact: a key within Lip cents of its nearest partial is open and lipped to pitch, any other is the next partial above lowered by the hand, and covering is the cents lowered over 120. Simplified: the tone is a closed form harmonic series whose brightness follows the breath, not a model of lips and air in a tube; the bell is a fixed shelf, peak and low-pass after three allpasses that only spread the peaks; the hand is a low-pass, a nasal band and a fall in level, so a note stopped fully is not raised by a half step as a hand pushed hard into a real bell can do; covering stays full below the fourth partial, where gaps are wider than a hand can close, and the pitch is right anyway; the distance is a duller horn and eight fixed answers a side, not a room. Choices, not measurements: 120 cents for a hand fully in, 60 cents for the thinnest lipped note, every filter figure of the hand and the bell, the brightness law and the levels by pitch, the rests of a slide, the rip's times, 28 cents of tremble, 14 cents of settling at the start of a note and half a cent of drift. Keys within two cents of each other sound as one horn, the newest. Tuned by measurement only: nobody has listened to it.
